title: "ADCP 1.1 tutorials"
---

## Generate a rotamer library for a non-standard amino acid

This tutorial shows how to generate a rotamer library (`.lib`) file for a non-standard amino
acid and use it in ADCP to dock peptides that contain it.

### Step 1: get the example files

Download [this zip file](https://github.com/sannerlab/downloads/releases/download/adcp-1.1/libGenExample.zip). It holds
dummy non-standard amino acids and randomly generated Dunbrack-like rotamer files. Make a
directory for the tutorial and unzip the file there:

```bash
mkdir -p ~/ADCP_examples/genLib
cd ~/ADCP_examples/genLib
wget https://github.com/sannerlab/downloads/releases/download/adcp-1.1/libGenExample.zip
unzip libGenExample.zip
```

The extracted `input` directory contains:

```
input/
├── libfiles
│   ├── FOO_random1.lib
│   └── SOO_random1.lib
├── pdbfiles
│   ├── D
│   │   ├── DFOO.pdb
│   │   └── DSOO.pdb
│   └── L
│       ├── FOO.pdb
│       └── SOO.pdb
└── rotamer_details.dat
```

### Step 2: extract rotamer information

```bash
extractRotamerInfo -l input/libfiles/ -p input/pdbfiles/ -i _random1.lib -r input/rotamer_details.dat -o rotamerinfo.py
```

Output:

```
file 'rotamerinfo.py' is created successfully. Run 'makeLibFile' to generate lib file.
```

### Step 3: generate the library file

```bash
makeLibFile -p input/pdbfiles -r input/rotamer_details.dat -t rotamerinfo.py -o my_foo_soo.lib
```

Output:

```
Using residue list from "input/rotamer_details.dat" for lib file generation!
Working on AA: FOO
Working on AA: SOO
Working on AA: DFOO
Working on AA: DSOO
ADCP acceptable lib file: 'my_foo_soo.lib' generated successfully
```

### Step 4: dock with the new library

Download the example [target file](https://github.com/sannerlab/downloads/releases/download/adcp-1.1/3Q47.trg) and run ADCP
with the new library (`-l`):

```bash
mkdir trialRun
cd trialRun
wget https://github.com/sannerlab/downloads/releases/download/adcp-1.1/3Q47.trg
adcp -T 3Q47.trg -s "F<FOO>R<SOO>&F<FOO>&R<SOO>G" -w testDir -o myfoo -l ../my_foo_soo.lib -O -n 2000 -m 5
```

The peptide uses all four residues of the new library, followed by a glycine (ADCP needs more
than 4 amino acids):

| In the sequence | Residue |
|---|---|
| `F<FOO>` | FOO, with a phenylalanine bead in the coarse model |
| `R<SOO>` | SOO, with an arginine bead |
| `&F<FOO>` | D-FOO: the `&` makes it D, and ADCP takes its rotamers from DFOO in the library |
| `&R<SOO>` | D-SOO, rotamers from DSOO |
| `G` | glycine |

The bead letters come from `input/rotamer_details.dat` (`FOO F DFOO …`, `SOO R DSOO …`). Write
them in upper case: with a user rotamer library, a lower-case bead letter in front of a residue
name makes the searches fail.

The run ends with a table of docked modes like this one; the values change from run to run:

```
mode |  affinity  | ref. | clust. | rmsd | energy | best |
     | (kcal/mol) | fnc  |  size  | stdv |  stdv  | run  |
-----+------------+------+--------+------+--------+------+
   1         -7.3      0.0       4      NA      NA    121
   2         -7.0      0.0       9      NA      NA    845
   3         -6.8      0.0      17      NA      NA    219
   4         -6.4      0.0       5      NA      NA    119
   5         -6.4      0.0       8      NA      NA    729
```

The docked poses are in `testDir/myfoo_out.pdb`, where residues 1 to 4 are named FOO, SOO, FOO
and SOO.

## Version 1.0 tutorials

The [ADCP 1.0 tutorials](../1.0/tutorials.qmd) (re-docking a linear peptide, re-docking a
cyclic peptide) were written for the 1.0 command line. In 1.1 the target file option is `-T`
instead of `-t` and the output files differ; see
[what changed in 1.1](../index.qmd#what-changed-in-version-1.1).
